extracted.intended_audience: general news readers (TODAY.com audience) interested in trending stories, consumer issues, and corporate behavior
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form trending news report that summarizes a corporate executive's public remarks, places them in context with data and company financials, and highlights public reaction via social media. Focus is on accessible reporting of a controversy for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline captures the main claim and controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline states the central remark and frames it as newsworthy controversy (example: "Kellogg CEO Says People Should Eat ‘Cereal for Dinner’ to Save Money").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise headline that presents the claim and signals the public reaction or controversy; the headline should make the story's focus immediately clear to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede summarizes the central fact and public sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening sentences summarize the CEO's suggestion and note the ongoing public response (example lede: "WK Kellogg CEO Gary Pilnick’s cost-saving suggestion of eating cereal for dinner has yet to win over consumers who are feeling the strain of grocery prices").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the most newsworthy element and the reaction up front so readers immediately understand both the claim and why it matters; avoid burying the controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute quotes to specific source, program and date
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify where and when the remark was made (example phrasing: "in an appearance on CNBC’s 'Squawk on the Street' Feb. 21").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always name the speaker, the media outlet or program, and date of appearance when reporting a direct remark to allow verification and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include verbatim quotes from the executive
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide direct, quoted text from the CEO to show precisely what was said (examples included multiple direct sentences from Pilnick about cereal pricing and occasions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact quotes to avoid mischaracterizing remarks; include enough surrounding sentences to capture nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting data with source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite relevant statistics and their sources (example: "more than 11% of disposable consumer income goes toward purchasing it, according to the most recent data available at the U.S. Department of Agriculture").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back claims and context with data from reputable sources and link or name the source so readers can check original data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report corporate financials and executive compensation with citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include company financial metrics and executive pay as context (examples: "Pilnick's annual salary is $1 million plus up to $4.4 million more in bonuses... per a filing with the SEC"; "The company reported $651 million in net sales as of Dec. 30").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant to the controversy, report concrete figures and cite filings or reports (SEC filings, earnings releases) to substantiate claims about profits/salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample and attribute public reaction via social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Show representative responses from platforms and attribute them (examples: quotes from X, Instagram, YouTube commenters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select representative, attributed social-media posts to illustrate public sentiment; identify the platform and avoid amplifying obviously inauthentic or unverified accounts without caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attempt and report on requests for company comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Note whether the company responded to requests for comment (example sentence: "WK Kellogg did not immediately respond to a request for comment.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attempt to contact the company for response; report the outcome (response, no response, or pending) to show balanced reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide broader interview context or counterpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Include additional context from the full interview or follow-up remarks (example: the article quotes the CEO saying "It's landing really well right now" and notes over 25% consumption outside breakfast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the wider context or any counter-arguments from the source to avoid selective quoting that skews meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use images with clear captions and credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a photo and caption identifying subject, occasion and credit (example caption: "WK Kellogg CEO Gary Pilnick on CNBC’s 'Squawk on the Street' Feb. 21. CNBC").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide image credits and a concise caption that reinforces the story context and source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline and reporter identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include author name and short reporter bio or role (example: "Randi Richardson is a reporter for NBC News' TODAY.com based in Brooklyn.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display a clear byline and, when useful, a one-line bio to establish reporter affiliation and locale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlink primary sources for reader verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed links to data sources, filings and original clips (examples: links to USDA data, SEC filing, the CNBC clip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to primary sources whenever possible so readers can verify claims and view original materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include publication timestamp and trending/updated indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Display when the piece was published and show whether it is part of a trending/updated feed (page shows "Feb. 26, 2024, 3:15 PM EST" and trending/updated labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make publication time and update status visible so readers know currency; label articles that are part of trending feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame story through public-interest lens and highlight perceived irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize why the remark matters to consumers (the article highlights perceived irony between CEO suggestions and corporate profits/salaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting controversies, explain the public-interest angle (e.g., economic pressure on consumers) and avoid editorializing without evidence; use data and attributed reactions to support framing.
